findings.title: The 'Q Let go to slingshot' prompt shows when the cable has no energy, so pressing Q does nothing
findings.problem:
The prompt 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' and the lit Q action button appear whenever rope.strain > 0.97 (src/ui/objectives.ts:79, src/ui/game-ui.ts:200). The slingshot's energy is a different number: energy = max(0, length − maxLength)² × 60 (src/sim/cable.ts:71). releasePlug only flings when energy > 1 (src/game.ts:259-261), which needs more than 0.13 m of overstretch (strain > 1.007 on the 19 m reel). The reel's spring force (cable.ts:78) then pulls Pip back to exactly maxLength within about 0.5 s of stopping, so the energy goes to 0 while the prompt stays on.

Measured:
- pg3 'idle': strain 1.045 after a sprint, then 0.7 s standing gives strain 1.0001. The prompt still says slingshot. Q gives fastestProp 0.02 and no pins move.
- pg2: the same thing after a 1.6 s camera zoom. Cable-24 shows nothing happened.
- Meeting mt4: the walk limit gives strain 1.022, then 1 s standing gives 1.000, Pip pulled 0.5 m back. The prompt reads 'Let go to slingshot the cable' (cable-113). Q or F only drops the plug.

The slingshot only works if the player presses Q while still holding sprint into the cable ('held' run: fastestProp 53.8). Nothing teaches that. A player who reads the prompt, stops and presses Q gets a thud. This is the game's signature cable moment (AGENTS 4), and the only text hint for it is wrong. It is a false prompt (DR-19) and makes the slingshot effectively undiscoverable (DR-06, R4B M9 still open).
findings.fix:
Make the stored charge, not the instantaneous stretch, drive both the prompt and the fling.

1. In `Rope` (src/sim/cable.ts), add a `charge` field. Each update while strain > 0.97: `charge = min(60, charge + dt*40*(strain-0.9))`. Otherwise: `charge *= exp(-dt/1.2)`.
2. Make `release()` return `max(energy, charge)` and reset both.
3. Show the Q prompt and light the Q button only when `charge > 8` (expose `rope.charge` in the snapshot).
4. Add a visible wind-up: the strain-HUD reel icon pulses, and the twang arcs (game.ts:299) grow with charge.

Result: standing at the limit 'loads' the cable within about 1 s, and Q always delivers once the prompt shows.
findings.verify: Add a routes.spec test, 'standing at the limit then Q still slingshots': pick up the plug, walk(9,3.7), advance(2.5, [KeyW, ShiftLeft]), then advance(1) with no keys, press Q, advance(0.05). Expect fastestProp > 2. A second assert: when the prompt text contains 'slingshot', Q always yields fastestProp > 2. Retake cable-22/23/24.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it in mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v1.mjs (Playground). I picked up the plug, walked to (9,3.7) and sprinted for 2.5 s, which gave strain 1.0446 and energy 43.1. After standing still for 0.6 s, strain was 1.0006 and energy 0.01, but the pill still read 'Q Let go to slingshot the cable' and the Q button was lit (verify-cable-01-stand-limit-prompt.jpg). Pressing Q gave fastestProp 0.02 and damage 0, with nothing visible. In Meeting (v2.mjs, deterministic over 2 runs), standing 1 s at the walk limit gave strain 1.0000 with the same slingshot prompt, and F only dropped the plug (verify-cable-06). In code, the prompt gates on strain>.97 (objectives.ts:79, game-ui.ts:200) and the fling on energy>1 (game.ts:261). The spring in cable.ts:79 (force=over*8) decays the overstretch with a time constant of about 0.125 s, so energy falls below 1 about 0.25 s after Pip stops. One correction to the problem text: it is not only 'while still holding sprint'. Holding W alone into the limit settles at over=4.2/8≈0.53 m, energy 16.5, and Q then gave fastestProp 20.55 (v1 walkW run). The real rule is 'Q works only while you keep pulling', and nothing on screen says that.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v1.mjs (stand0.3: strain 1.0006, E 0.01, prompt slingshot, Q fastest 0.02; walkW: E 16.54, Q fastest 20.55; sprintNow: E 43.1, Q fastest 53.77)
src/sim/cable.ts:79 (pull force=min(35,over*8): equilibrium overstretch is speed/8)
findings.fix_correction: The charge idea is workable, but its arithmetic doesn't match its claim. With charge += dt*40*(strain-0.9), standing at strain 1.0 adds 4 per second, so the threshold of 8 is reached after about 2 s, not about 1 s. It also invents energy that the rope model says isn't there: at rest the spring force is 0. A simpler fix that is truthful at this level: (1) Show the Q prompt and light the Q button only when rope.energy > 1, i.e. while Pip is actually pulling past the length (over > 0.13 m). Otherwise keep 'F Drop the plug', or better, show no text and let Pip lean and dig in. (2) Keep a short grace window in Rope: peak = max(peak*exp(-dt/0.35), energy), and have release() return peak. Then letting go of W and pressing Q within about 0.3 s still flings. (3) Optional: while strain > .97 and energy < 1, pulse the reel icon to say 'pull harder' with no words. Verify: v1.mjs 'stand0.3' shows no slingshot prompt, and 'walkW' plus Q still gives fastestProp > 2.

findings.title: The slingshot has no recoil: the plug and cable never snap back, props just get an invisible kick
findings.problem:
When the slingshot fires:
- The plug only moves 15% of the way toward the last bend (lerp 0.15, src/game.ts:262). The cable is redrawn in the same place.
- Props within 1.1 m of the cable get an impulse directed away from the anchor (game.ts:257), with a screen shake of at most 0.5.
- There is no hitstop: plugFlash has 0.09 s (game.ts:249), the slingshot has none. There is no whip sound shaped to the motion, and no cable movement.

In cable-26/27/28, the 'slingshot' reads as the cable going white and a chair and cone sliding a little. The cable itself, the star, does nothing. In cable-32/33 (pins), most of the strike came from dragging the pins during the sprint (pinsDown 2 before Q), not from the release.

In Good Job!, the satisfaction comes from watching the stretched cord whip back through the room. Here the cause (a stretched cable) and the effect (things fly) aren't connected on screen, so it doesn't read as a slingshot and isn't rewarding (DR-06, DR-11).
findings.fix:
Animate the recoil and hit props from the moving plug.

1. On release with energy > 1, start a 0.35 s recoil: tween `plugPosition` back along the current route (ropePoints, from the end toward the last bend and then the anchor) by `min(3, over*4 + 1.5)` m, with an ease-out curve.
2. Each recoil frame, sweep a 0.6 m-radius capsule from the plug's previous position to its new one. Give any prop it touches `impulse = clamp(energy*.22, 4, 30)`. Direct it along the recoil direction (toward the anchor) plus 0.5 up.
3. Add `hitstop = .06` at the start, and a whip sound (rising noise sweep 400→2500 Hz over 0.15 s).
4. Spawn 6 dust puffs along the cable as it slackens.
5. Keep the 1.1 m 'whip' kick for props lying on the cable, but use the same direction.

Put this in one shared helper used by both Game.releasePlug and LunchRuntime.release.
findings.verify: Take a frame sequence at +0, +0.1, +0.2 and +0.35 s after Q in the pg3 'held' setup. The plug should visibly travel at least 2 m toward the reel. Spec: after Q, snapshot plug or rope length drops by at least 1.5 m within 0.4 s, and fastestProp > 2.
findings.verify_reason: In code, releasePlug only lerps the plug 15% toward the last bend (game.ts:262), slingshot() applies one static impulse to props within 1.1 m of the frozen route (game.ts:255-257), and there is no hitstop (plugFlash sets one, game.ts:249; slingshot does not). I reproduced the sprint-then-Q sequence (verify-cable-03-sling-0s.jpg, verify-cable-04-sling-0.15s.jpg). The cable stays in exactly the same place and turns white, and the plug lands at Pip's feet, so the prompt immediately says 'Pick up the plug'. A chair and the cones slide a little. Route length only drops from 19.85 to 19.39 m, then creeps back to 19.71 m. Nothing on screen connects the stretched cable to the props moving.

findings.title: The cable passes straight through the box or shelf Pip presses the plug against
findings.problem:
simulateCable drops any furniture obstacle whose padded AABB contains the plug position or the anchor (src/game.ts:279). The plug is simulated 0.65 m in front of Pip (game.ts:267). Walking up to a crate stack or bookshelf therefore puts the plug inside that prop's box, the prop is removed from the obstacle list, and the cable is routed and drawn straight through it. Any wraps on that prop also vanish, so the bend can jump.

- cable-124 (zoom 9, Playground): the hose and the held plug go into the middle of the crate stack beside Pip.
- cable-17 (socket orbit): the cable runs through the candy-block bookshelf next to the lamp.

This breaks DR-73 ('wraps around obstacles instead of clipping them'). It happens in the most-watched spot, right next to Pip, every time the player hugs furniture, which dense rooms (AGENTS 3) make constant.
findings.fix:
Push the end out of the box instead of deleting the obstacle.

1. In simulateCable, for each furniture AABB that contains `plugPosition`, keep the obstacle. Clamp the rope end used for routing to the nearest face plus CORNER (0.12 m): move along the axis of smallest penetration.
2. Use the clamped point as `end` in `rope.update`, and keep `plugPosition` itself for snapping.
3. Do the same for the anchor (or simply never spawn clutter on the anchor).
4. Pull the plug's visual position back to the clamped point, so the glove doesn't sink into the crate.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/pg8.mjs (walk into the crate stack at (-2,4.6)) and check cable-124. The hose must bend around the crate's corner. Unit test in src/sim/cable.test.ts: an end inside an obstacle gives a route whose segments don't intersect that obstacle.
findings.verify_reason: The code mechanism is real. game.ts:279 drops any furniture AABB that contains plugPosition, and the plug is 0.65 m ahead of Pip (game.ts:267), so pushing into a desk or bookshelf removes it as an obstacle and unwraps any bends on it. But the cited screenshots show other causes. cable-124: the crate stack is made of kind 'box' (playground.ts:11), mass 2 (prefabs.ts:10). Boxes never enter the obstacle list because of the mass>=3 filter (game.ts:273), which is finding 9, not this rule. cable-17/17b: Pip faces the lamp, away from the shelf (cable-17), so the plug isn't inside it. That candy-block 'shelf' is a toppled bookshelf (clutter.ts:42; 2 x 1.8 x 0.45). The AABB at game.ts:276-277 uses only matrix elements [0],[8] and [2],[10] and leaves out the height column ([4],[6]). A bookshelf lying on its back therefore becomes a sliver about 0.1 m thick, and the cable crosses its full 1.8 m length. That is a separate real bug the reviewer didn't identify. I didn't reproduce the plug-inside case itself. Its visible effect is mostly the last 0.3 m by the glove, unless a wrap gets dropped, so P2.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:276-277 (AABB ignores the prop's height axis: rotation elements [4]/[6] missing)
mockups/review5/shots/cable-17-pg-at-socket-close-orbit.jpg (Pip faces away from the toppled shelf)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the face-clamp idea for plugPosition. Separately, fix the AABB so tipped props keep their footprint. In simulateCable, compute hx=|e0|*w/2+|e4|*h/2+|e8|*d/2+.05 and hz=|e2|*w/2+|e6|*h/2+|e10|*d/2+.05 (the [w,h,d] from prefabs size). Retake cable-17 after knocking the bookshelf over: the hose must bend around it.

findings.title: REGRESSION / still open (P3): the cable runs through Pip's legs and body to reach the glove
findings.fix:
Route the last metre around Pip's body.

1. In drawCable (and in the Lunch render loop at lunch-runtime.ts:315), when holding, take the incoming route direction `d` (last bend → Pip). Insert a waypoint at Pip's hip on the side the cable arrives from: `pip + perp(d)*0.35 − d*0.25`, at y 0.5. Then rise from there to the glove.
2. Alternatively, switch to a drag pose: hold the plug in the trailing hand at the hip, behind Pip (plugPosition = pip − forward*0.45 for routing). Grab-drag reads better and matches Good Job's cable carry.
3. After plugging in, make the socket side end at the socket face. Keep Pip's win-pose spot 0.6 m to the side of the cable line (winFocus, game.ts:398).
findings.verify: Retake cable-18 (the win), cable-41 and cable-84 at zoom 9 from the front and from the back (orbit ±700). No hose pixels should overlap Pip's legs or torso. A check in pg1: the distance from each cablePath sample to Pip's capsule axis must be > 0.3 m, except for the final 0.4 m into the glove.
findings.verify_reason: Visible in cable-19b-crop-win-legs.jpg: the gold cable runs between Pip's boots into the socket. In cable-41-pg-wrap-pillar-close.jpg, the hose rises through Pip's legs and hip to the glove in front. In code, cablePath redraws the last route segment straight to the glove position (game.ts:12, b=end for the last segment). The route ends at plugPosition, 0.65 m ahead (game.ts:267), and the cable trails from behind, so the final rise crosses Pip's body. This breaks DR-73.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:12 (last route segment's end replaced by the glove point)

findings.title: Lunch cables never wrap furniture: they pass straight through tables, chairs, coworkers, bots and the dolly
findings.problem:
LunchRuntime routes every cable with `cable.rope.update(end, g.level.obstacles)` (src/lunch-runtime.ts:243), which means walls only. The furniture-corner logic that Playground and Meeting use (game.ts:273-282) isn't applied.

- cable-131: a taut thin lead (strain 0.96) runs diagonally across the lounge, through the round table, a blue chair, a pink coworker and the bot lane.
- cable-89: the thin lead passes through a cleaner bot.
- cable-84: the thick cable runs under and through its own dolly.

Lunch is the room with the most cables (4 plus splitters). The cable rule (AGENTS 4: 'wraps') and the routing lesson (keep leads out of the bots' path and the door) depend on cables lying around objects. Here routing is only about walls, and props can't be used to snag or wrap a lead.
findings.fix:
Share the furniture-corner logic.

1. Factor the furniture-obstacle builder in Game.simulateCable (game.ts:270-282) into `furnitureNear(route, exclude)`, returning `Obstacle[]` plus the wrapped set.
2. Call it per cable in LunchRuntime.step: `cable.rope.update(end, [...g.level.obstacles, ...furnitureNear(cable.points)])`. Exclude the dolly, tray and bots, which are dynamic and would fight.
3. For NPCs and bots, push them gently aside instead, or let the cable lie under them visually by raising the hose 0.12 m over their footprint in cablePath.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/ln2.mjs and retake cable-131. The thin lead should bend around the lounge table and chairs. Spec in lunch-rules.spec.ts: drag thin-2 past the lounge table, then check that snapshot.lunch.cablePoints['thin-2'] has at least one bend near the table's corners.
findings.verify_reason: lunch-runtime.ts:243 calls rope.update(end, g.level.obstacles), which means walls only. simulateCable (with the furniture logic) never runs on Lunch (game.ts:348). cable-131 shows the orange taut thin lead crossing the round lounge table, a blue chair and the pink coworker. cable-84 shows the thick hose passing under and through the dolly's deck.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:348 (Lunch runs lunch.step instead of simulateCable)
findings.fix_correction: When reusing the furniture builder in Lunch, exclude more than the dolly, tray and bots. Leave out cable bridges (kind 'bridge', mass 3, which would pass the mass>=3 filter): cables are meant to lie ON them (bridgeNear, lunch-runtime.ts:206-208). Wrapping a bridge would break the wet-cable/bridge lesson. Also leave out splitters, the supply carts and the capacitor cart (they carry ports, so a cable end sits inside their boxes), the mop and the door leaves. Use an allowlist of solid furniture kinds (table, chair, sofa, shelf, cabinet, desk, cooler, vending).

findings.title: Joining the coupler and second reel makes no visible change to the cable
findings.problem:
The clean Meeting route is the only place the game teaches 'join two leads to get more length'. When the coupler and then the extension reel are attached (attachNear, src/game.ts:233-236; or E with a held part, :207), both props are consumed (`consume(p)` hides them). rope.maxLength jumps from 23.2 to 37.2 m, and the only feedback is a confetti burst and the HUD bar dropping from about 60% to about 35%.

The cable stays one seamless hose from the server-closet reel (cable-71 → cable-72 → cable-73). There's no second reel, no joint, and no new section. After the join, the server reel's spool reads against 37.2 m of capacity it doesn't hold (cable-74).

The player can't see why the cable now reaches, or that it is two cables. That works against AGENTS 4 (finite length readable) and DR-26 (concept taught by a visible physical act), and against DR-46 (cable state readable without text).
findings.fix:
Make the join physical and visible.

1. Don't hide the extension reel. On attach, snap it to the plug's current point and record `joinAt = rope.length` (the arc length where the leads meet).
2. In drawCable, draw a coupler mesh (the coupler prop's model, oriented by the curve tangent) at `curve.getPointAt(min(1, joinAt/len))`.
3. Tint the section past the joint differently: a second jacket colour, or the thick cable's ink bands at a narrower spacing (hoseGeometry's `bands`).
4. Drive two spools:
   - The server reel shows `left = 1 − min(len, 23.2)/23.2`.
   - The extension reel, either carried along at the joint or left on the mail cart with a lead, shows its own 14 m.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/cable/mt2.mjs. In cable-73, a coupler joint and a differently striped section must be visible at Pip's position. Then walk 10 m on: the joint stays at the attach spot and only the extension's spool shrinks. Update the spec 'holding the plug, F at the mail cart…' to assert that a joint position is in the snapshot.
findings.verify_reason: attachNear (game.ts:233-236) and the held-part path (game.ts:207) call consume(), which hides the prop and disables its body, then set rope.maxLength=level.length+14. In cable-71 the yellow extension reel is in Pip's hand. In cable-73 it is gone and the hose is one seamless white cable, with only the HUD bar dropping. The spool scale (game.ts:292) divides by the new 37.2 m maxLength, so the server reel's spool shows capacity it doesn't hold. The one 'join two leads' lesson has no physical trace.

findings.title: In Lunch the cable's length almost never matters, and the slingshot and strain beats are unreachable
findings.problem:
Lunch's loose leads are 32, 30 and 32 m (thin) and 30 m (thick) (src/lunch-runtime.ts:61), in a room about 32 m wide.

- Sprinting thin-2 from Supply A along the corridor into the far north-east corner peaked at strain 0.963 (ln2 log; cable-131).
- Sprinting thin-1 east along the corridor reached 0.927 (ln1).
- Q then threw nothing (fastestProp 1.9, then 0).
- The thick cable slows Pip to 0.65× (game.ts:318), so it can't be sprint-overstretched either.

The Lunch-specific cable code also has none of the main cable's feel: no twang arcs, jitter or corner sparks (only Game.drawCable has them, game.ts:296-300), no hitstop, and no auto-whip off corners (game.ts:286).

So the third cable floor, the longest job, drops the 'finite length, strain, slingshot' pillar (AGENTS 4; DR-05, DR-06). Strain colours never appear in a normal solve, and the cables behave like free extension leads.
findings.fix:
Make length a real constraint in Lunch and give it the same feel as the other floors.

1. Shorten the leads so the long runs need planning:
   - thin-1 and thin-3 to about 18 m: they reach the kitchen and fridge from A or B, not the lift;
   - thin-2 to about 24 m: A to the conveyor via the corridor is about 21 m, so a sloppy route goes yellow or orange;
   - thick to about 22 m.
   Check against the lunch.spec.ts routes, which should stay at strain < 0.9.
2. Move the bite, jitter and twang block (game.ts:296-300) into a shared `cableFeel(points, rope, group)` helper, and call it from LunchRuntime.render for the held cable.
3. Use the shared recoil from the slingshot-recoil finding for release.
4. Put one fling target within reach of a stretched lead: for example, the stack of empty trays by the conveyor, which a thin lead from A overstretched past the corridor bend can whip.
findings.verify: Run lunch.spec.ts: the intended solution must still pass. A new spec: drag thin-2 from A toward the lift room with a sprint, expect strain > 1 and a slingshot fastestProp > 2 after Q. Screenshot: the held thin lead shows orange or red with twang arcs at the corridor corner.
findings.verify_reason: In code, the leads are 32, 30, 32 (thin) and 30 (thick) m (lunch-runtime.ts:61) in a 33x20 m room (lunch.ts:15). Lunch never calls drawCable or simulateCable (game.ts:348, 431), so there are no jitter, twang, spark or corner-whip effects. LunchRuntime.release has no hitstop or recoil (lunch-runtime.ts:199-203). The reviewer's ln1/ln2 logs show peak strain 0.927 and 0.963 even when sprinting to the far corner, and Q flinging nothing. I didn't re-run the Lunch sprint myself, but the geometry backs it up: the farthest reachable point from Supply A (-13,3) is about 31.6 m in a straight line.
extra_evidence: tests/lunch.spec.ts:34-38 (thin-1 carries the lift feed to the capacitor cart)
findings.fix_correction: The proposed lengths would break the intended solution. In tests/lunch.spec.ts:34-38, thin-1 is the lift feed: it is moved from the fridge out through the kitchen door to (10,1) and the capacitor cart at the winch (about 11.3,-4.4), a run of roughly 28-30 m from Supply A. thin-1 can't drop to 18 m. Measure each lead's strain at the end of every lunch.spec route first (log snapshot().lunch cable lengths), then set each length to about 1.08-1.12x its longest intended route. Thin-2 (A to conveyor through the door, about 21 m) at about 24 m is fine, and so is thick (about 17.6 m to the kitchen post) at about 20-22 m. Keep thin-1 at about 32 m, or reroute the lift feed in the spec.

findings.title: The thick-cable dolly isn't the cable's source; it rides 1.3 m beside Pip and the cable passes through it (DR-74 still open)
findings.problem:
While the thick cable is held, the dolly with the big yellow drum is driven toward Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away (src/lunch-runtime.ts:237). The hose itself is drawn from Supply B straight to Pip's glove and ignores the drum.

- cable-83: the dolly sits between the camera and Pip's legs.
- cable-84: the striped cable runs under the dolly's deck and wheels, not off the drum.
- cable-136: the dolly is left behind in the corridor while the cable lies elsewhere.

The prop that looks like 'the reel of thick cable' has nothing to do with the cable's length or path. It parks next to Pip and blocks him. This is known as DR-74 (rule says P1), and is still open at HEAD.
findings.fix:
Put the dolly on the cable path.

1. Sample the held thick cable's route at arc length `max(0, len − 2.2)` and drive the dolly toward that point, so it trails 2.2 m behind along the cable. That keeps it out of the camera line by construction.
2. Split the drawn hose: supply → dolly drum (slack) and drum → glove (taut, showing strain).
3. Spin the drum with paid-out length, and scale a wound-cable cylinder on the drum the way the reel spool works (game.ts:292), so the drum shows the length left.
findings.verify: Retake research-art-38/39 and cable-83/84 at the default camera and orbited 180°. The dolly must be at least 2 m behind Pip along the cable, and the cable must visibly leave the drum. Check in ln2.mjs: the distance from the dolly to Pip is at least 1.9 m throughout the thick drag.
findings.verify_reason: lunch-runtime.ts:237 drives the dolly toward Pip whenever it is more than 1.3 m away. The hose is routed from Supply B to the glove and never touches the drum (lunch-runtime.ts:239-243, 312-315). In cable-84 the dolly sits right beside Pip and the striped hose runs under its deck. In cable-136 the dolly is left behind. This matches the open DR-74 (mockups/review5/RULES.md:459, which cites this exact line).
findings.fix_correction: Account for the plug offset. The held end is 0.6 m ahead of Pip (lunch-runtime.ts:241), so sampling at len-2.2 leaves the dolly only about 1.6 m behind Pip. Sample at arc length max(0, len-2.8) to meet DR-74's 2 m.

findings.title: A cable at rest is cream on a cream floor, less saturated than the floor; yellow strain is lost on Lunch's wood
findings.problem:
The hose's rest colour is #f5f1dc (src/render/actors.ts:65, STRAIN), and a dropped or slack cable is drawn at strain 0.3 (game.ts:294).

On the Playground concrete (#d8cdb8, decor.ts:84), PIL samples on cable-122 give:
- the lit top of the cable: luma 232, saturation 0.09;
- the floor next to it: luma 191–212, saturation 0.17;
- the cable's shaded side: luma 185, the same as the floor.

So for most of a run the cable is the least saturated object near Pip and reads mainly through its outline (cable-10, cable-40, cable-122/123). DR-53 says the cable should be the most saturated thing near Pip.

In Lunch, the yellow strain band (#ffd451) on the honey wood floor nearly disappears (cable-130). The thin leads (radius 0.075, #ece8dc) are pale hairlines at the game camera (cable-134; LR5 still partly open).

Strain reads well from orange up (cable-12, cable-21, cable-64), so this is polish for the rest and yellow states.
findings.fix:
Keep the white → yellow → orange → red ramp (AGENTS 4), but give the jacket an ink identity.

1. Pass `bands:true` with a thin stripe for the hero cable: a 0.05 m ink band every 0.6 m, using hoseGeometry's band code with a smaller duty cycle.
2. Raise the outline weight on the hose: the material `size` from 0.982 to about 0.975.
3. Add a soft contact-shadow decal under the hose: a dark ribbon 0.3 m wide at 20% opacity.
4. For Lunch, darken the yellow stop to #ffc21a, or outline-tint it on wood floors.
5. Raise thin-lead radius to 0.085, as the Good Job hose readability suggests.
findings.verify: Re-measure cable-122 and cable-123 with PIL. The cable's edge-band luma should differ from the adjacent floor by at least 40, and the cable crop's mean chroma should exceed the floor's. Lunch: a crop of a yellow-strain thin lead on wood shows its ink bands at the game camera.
findings.verify_reason: The colours and code are as cited: the rest colour is #f5f1dc (actors.ts:65), slack is drawn at strain .3 (game.ts:294), and the thin lead radius is .075 (lunch-runtime.ts:315). In cable-123 the cream hose reads mostly through its dark outline and shading against the beige floor. In cable-130 the yellow thin lead on honey wood is low contrast but still readable up close. I couldn't re-measure the PIL numbers (PIL isn't available in isolated Python here). Note that AGENTS 4 itself makes the rest colour white, so this is polish.
findings.fix_correction: Two parts of the fix are technically wrong. (1) glossyToon's `size` (actors.ts:9-12, hoseMaterial at actors.ts:78) is the specular-highlight edge (uniform specEdge), not the outline weight. Changing .982 to .975 only resizes the highlight. To thicken the hose outline, set the OutlineEffect parameters on the hose material (material.userData.outlineParameters={thickness:~0.006}), the same mechanism game.ts:95 uses to hide outlines. (2) Don't add ink bands to the thin Lunch leads. In Lunch, bands are the signifier of the thick 10 A cable (bands: cable.rating>3, lunch-runtime.ts:315), and striping thin leads would blur the rating lesson. Use the contact-shadow ribbon and the larger radius instead.

findings.title: The cable lies through light props (plants, cones, bins) and through props past the 20-obstacle cap
findings.problem:
Only props with mass ≥ 3 that sit within 1.2 m of the current route, capped at the nearest 20, become cable obstacles (src/game.ts:273-274).

- Plants (mass 2), cones (1), bins (0.5), reels (2), mops, wedges and lamps under 3 are ignored outright.
- Light props are only shoved when strain > 0.88 (game.ts:333).

At normal strain the hose passes straight through plant pots and cones. In the dense Meeting and Playground, the 20-prop cap can also drop heavier props along a long route. playground-play-61 shows the taut cable passing through a beanbag (mass 4). The meeting boardroom glass front (decor.ts:144-145) is `solid` for Pip but isn't a cable obstacle, so the gold cable cuts through its corner rail (cable-67, cable-68).
findings.fix:
1. Light props: at any strain, apply a small lateral impulse (about 0.4 × dt × mass) pushing them perpendicular out of the hose when their centre is within 0.25 m plus half their size of a cable segment. The cable then nudges pots and cones aside.
2. Raise the furniture cap from 20 to 32, but only count props within 3 m of Pip or of an existing bend.
3. Add the two boardroom glass-front spans to `meeting.obstacles`, or let `solid()` take a `cable:true` flag that registers an Obstacle:
   - `{id:'glass-front-w', minX:9.3, maxX:11, minZ:-2.07, maxZ:-1.93}`
   - `{id:'glass-front-e', minX:13.8, maxX:16.5, minZ:-2.07, maxZ:-1.93}`
findings.verify: Retake cable-67/68 (the meeting plug-in): the cable must enter through the doorway (x 11–13.8). Playground: drag the cable through the plant cluster by the north wall at strain 0.5. In a zoom-9 screenshot, no hose passes through a pot, and the pots have moved.
findings.verify_reason: In code, only props with mass>=3 enter the obstacle list (game.ts:273), and boxes are mass 2 (prefabs.ts:10). Light props are shoved only at strain>.88 (game.ts:333). The Meeting glass front is a physics collider only (decor.ts:144-145; solid() at decor.ts:21-24 creates no Obstacle), and meeting.obstacles (meeting.ts:34-35) lacks it. cable-68 shows the gold cable passing under the glass front's bottom rail instead of through the doorway. Raising to P1: the Playground's designed obstacle course is crate stacks of kind 'box' (playground.ts:9-11, 'to drag the cable through'), and the cable passes straight through them right at Pip's glove (cable-124, which the reviewer attributed to finding 2). That is the tutorial room breaking the 'wraps around obstacles' rule (AGENTS 4, DR-73) in its most-seen spot. The toppled-bookshelf AABB bug (see finding 2) also adds to this.
findings.fix_correction: Besides nudging light props, let floor-standing boxes count as wrap obstacles: lower the filter to mass>=2 for kind 'box', or add a per-prefab `wrap:true` flag, and keep the y<1.8 test so stacked tops don't double count. Also include the height axis in the AABB (|e4|*h/2, |e6|*h/2) so tipped props keep their footprint. After adding the glass-front obstacles, rerun tests/routes.spec.ts. The Meeting single-reel and coupler routes have very thin length margins (see finding 10), and a corner wrap at x=11 adds length.

findings.title: Meeting: the single reel's walking reach sits on the edge of the snap radius, so 'Plug in' flickers and the spec is flaky
findings.problem:
Walking (no sprint) along the spec route and then holding D leaves Pip 2.24 m (mt1) or 2.29 m (mt4) from the socket. The snap accepts 2.2 m (pos distance − 0.6 < 1.6, game.ts:205).

- In mt1 the prompt said 'Plug in' at the walk limit (cable-64).
- In mt4, standing 1 s let the reel's spring pull Pip back to 2.79 m. The prompt flipped to the dead 'Let go to slingshot' (cable-113), and F just dropped the plug.

tests/routes.spec.ts:33 asserts > 2.3 m. That is a 0.01–0.06 m margin, so the test is flaky, and so is what players experience.

The intended lesson ('the reel is too short: join a second one, or overstretch at a sprint') depends on a clear miss. Nothing in the world hints that sprinting gains length (R4B M9, still partial).
findings.fix:
1. Make the miss unambiguous: shorten the server reel to about 22.0 m (meeting.ts:33, `length`), so walking stops at least 3 m short. Retune the sprint overstretch by raising the spring clearance in Rope.pull (cable.ts:78, `*8`), so a sprint still reaches, or keep the 23.2 m reel and move the strip spot 1 m further east.
2. Hint the sprint: at strain > 0.97 while walking, show 'Shift Sprint to stretch it' once. Or animate Pip leaning and digging in with dust puffs, which already exist for sprinting (7ea4544).
3. Make the spec assert at least 3 m.
findings.verify: Run the 'meeting single reel only reaches when overstretched at a sprint' spec 10 times. It must pass 10/10. In mt4.mjs, the 'spec walk limit' distance must be ≥ 3 m, and the prompt there must not say 'Plug in'.
findings.verify_reason: I replicated the spec route in mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v2.mjs: placeStrip, backToReel, F, route [-8,-5],[-1,-1.5],[6,-1.2], then advance(2,['KeyD']). Over 2 runs, with and without fullfx, it deterministically left Pip 2.288 m from the socket at strain 1.022. tests/routes.spec.ts:33 asserts toBeGreaterThan(2.3), so with this replica the assertion would fail outright, not just flake. After standing 1 s, Pip is 2.792 m away and the prompt is the dead 'Let go to slingshot the cable' (verify-cable-06). F just drops the plug (not connected). The snap threshold is pos-.6<1.6 → 2.2 m (game.ts:205), so the walk-versus-sprint gap is only about 0.09 m. The structural cause: sprint only gains (6.8-4.2)/8 ≈ 0.33 m over walking (cable.ts:79).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-cable/v2.mjs (walk limit dist 2.288 both runs; stood 1 s 2.792)
findings.fix_correction: 'Raise the spring clearance (*8)' is ambiguous. The overstretch is speed/k, so to give the sprint more reach than the walk you must lower k in Rope.pull (cable.ts:79). For example, k≈3 gives a walk-to-sprint gap of 2.6/k ≈ 0.87 m, and then shortening the reel by about 0.8 m makes the walk miss at about 3 m while the sprint still reaches. Keep strain<1.12 at the plug (game.ts:205): 23.2*1.12=26 m. Re-tune the slingshot energy (over²·60), which grows with the larger overstretch. Skip the 'Shift Sprint to stretch it' text: AGENTS asks for a minimal text HUD. Use the visual dig-in or lean plus sprint dust.

findings.title: The slingshot direction is opposite between floors, and light litter is launched at more than 50 m/s
findings.problem:
Direction: Game.slingshot pushes props away from the anchor, `v = pos − anchor` (src/game.ts:257). LunchRuntime.release pushes them toward the anchor, `v = anchor − p`, as its comment says ('back toward its anchor', lunch-runtime.ts:198-202). The same key and the same prompt fling things in opposite directions on different floors. Physically, a released stretched cable recoils toward the reel.

Speed: the impulse is `min(energy*.22, 45) * min(1, mass/4 + .25)`, so a 0.05 kg paper or 0.15 kg mug gets roughly a quarter of the full impulse. The pg3 'held' release measured fastestProp 53.8 m/s. Props at that speed can tunnel through the 0.35 m walls and read as noise, not as comedy.
findings.fix:
Use one shared `whip(points, anchor, energy)` helper for both floors.

1. Direction: toward the anchor along the nearest segment's tangent, plus 0.5 up.
2. Speed: clamp each prop's resulting speed, with `impulse = min(impulse, mass*14)` (at most 14 m/s).
3. Enable CCD on light props for 1 s after a whip (`body.enableCcd(true)`).
findings.verify: Spec: after the pg3 'held' release, fastestProp is between 6 and 15. A prop at the cable's midpoint moves toward the reel (its position delta has a negative dot product with (prop − anchor)) on both Playground and Lunch.
findings.verify_reason: The direction mismatch is real. game.ts:257 uses v=pos-anchor (away from the reel), while lunch-runtime.ts:201 uses v=anchor-p (toward it, as its comment at :198 says). Speed is real too: I measured fastestProp 53.77 m/s in the sprint-then-Q release (v1.mjs). With impulse=min(E*.22,45)*min(1,m/4+.25), a 0.05 kg paper gets about 2.5 N·s, which is about 50 m/s. The tunnelling worry is overstated, though: prop bodies already use setCcdEnabled(p.mass<4) (game.ts:123).
findings.fix_correction: Drop step 3 (enable CCD for 1 s): CCD is already on for every prop under 4 kg (game.ts:123). Keep the shared whip helper, the toward-anchor direction and the speed clamp (impulse<=mass*14).

findings.title: The strain thresholds are defined three times and disagree; the HUD meter, hose colour and prompt don't line up
findings.problem:
There are separate strain definitions that don't match:
- src/sim/cable.ts:83, `strainColor`: bands at 0.7, 0.85 and 0.97. It is unit-tested (cable.test.ts:8) and imported but unused by game.ts and lunch-runtime.ts.
- src/render/actors.ts:65, `STRAIN`: a ramp with stops at 0.55, 0.72, 0.86 and 1.0. This one actually colours the hose.
- objectives.ts:79 and game-ui.ts:200: the slingshot prompt and button at 0.97.
- game-ui.ts:186: the HUD bar scaled `strain/1.15`.
- audio.ts:46: the hum starting at 0.7.

On top of that, the hose colour along the length is `strain*(0.6 + 0.4u)` (game.ts:304). At strain 1.0 the reel end is still white and only the hand end is red, while the HUD bar is at 87%.

The player gets three slightly different 'how close am I' signals. The tested colour table isn't the one rendered.
findings.fix:
1. Keep one table, `STRAIN_BANDS = {yellow:.72, orange:.86, red:1.0}`, in src/sim/cable.ts.
2. Build the actors.ts ramp from it and delete the unused `strainColor` imports.
3. Drive the HUD bar's colour stops from the same table, and scale the bar as `strain/1.0`, clamped, with a red 'over' overflow segment.
4. Show the prompt and button only on the stored charge (see the false-prompt finding).
5. Update cable.test.ts to test the rendered ramp.
findings.verify: Unit test: `strainAt(.72)` = yellow, `strainAt(.86)` = orange, `strainAt(1)` = red, and the HUD stop CSS variables match. Screenshot at strain 0.86: the HUD bar fill colour and the hand end of the hose are the same orange.
findings.verify_reason: strainColor (cable.ts:83, bands .7/.85/.97) is imported at game.ts:24 and lunch-runtime.ts:6 but never called. A grep finds only the imports and cable.test.ts:8. The hose uses STRAIN (actors.ts:65, stops .55/.72/.86/1). The HUD bar is strain/1.15 (game-ui.ts:186), so it reads 87% at strain 1. The prompt and button use .97 (objectives.ts:79, game-ui.ts:200), and the hum starts at .7 (audio.ts:46). The hose ramp strain*(.6+.4u) (game.ts:304) puts the reel end at 0.6 at strain 1, which is still almost white on the STRAIN ramp.

notes.fun:
What works:
- Dragging the reel cable through a dense room is the best thing in the game. At the game camera the hose is fat (0.2 m), strain shows as a gradient that warms toward Pip's hand (cable-11/12, cable-62→65), and near the limit it jitters, throws twang arcs and sparks at the corner it bites (cable-22).
- Coworkers along a taut cable pop '!' bubbles (cable-64/65), and the reel's spring physically pulls Pip back, which feels elastic and physical.
- Wrapping a pillar and walking back to unwrap it is clean: bends are added at real corners and removed in reverse (pg5 log, cable-40..44).
- The Playground pins can be knocked over by dragging a taut cable through them (pg4: 2 down during the sprint, 3 moved after Q).

What lets it down:
- The slingshot, the signature moment, is weak and hard to find. The prompt appears when Q will do nothing (standing at the limit), it only works mid-sprint, and when it fires the cable and plug don't recoil: props just get kicked, with no hitstop.
- Lunch, the third cable floor, has leads so long that strain and slingshot never come up, and none of the twang feel.
- The meeting coupler and extension join is invisible.

Compared with Good Job's cable levels, the drag is there; the release payoff and the satisfaction of a cable that visibly runs out and joins are not.
notes.playability:
Picking up, dragging and plugging in are forgiving and reliable:
- The plug snaps from 2.2 m (game.ts:205).
- The clean Playground route finishes in about 15 s (pg1, won at 15.1 s, A/A/A).
- Meeting coupler then extension via F works, with a helpful 'Attach the coupler first' prompt (cable-71).

Problems:
- The Q/slingshot prompt is false most of the time it shows (DR-19).
- The Meeting single-reel reach sits on the snap boundary (2.24–2.29 m vs 2.2), so 'Plug in' flickers and the spec margin is about 0.05 m.
- The cable has no physical presence for Pip: walking or jumping over it does nothing (pg5/pg6). That is acceptable, but a small step-up or stumble would sell it.
- The automatic whip when a taut rope comes off a corner (game.ts:286) is a nice hidden reward, but nothing in the world points to it.
- All scripts closed their browsers except pg7.mjs, which crashed on a bad evaluate before g.close(). Node exited, so Playwright should have reaped it, but leftover chrome-headless-shell processes were visible, possibly from other reviewers.
notes.teaching:
The cable teaches length and routing honestly in the Playground. The spool shrinks as cable pays out (game.ts:292), and the HUD reel meter and strain bar back it up (cable-10, cable-44).

Weak spots:
- In the Meeting the length lesson ('join a second lead') has no visual: the extension simply disappears into the cable.
- In Lunch, length barely constrains anything, so 'cable rating' and 'route' are taught by heat, water and door rules, not by the cable's finiteness.
- The idle route hint still flows cyan dots along an open circuit and through props (cable-54; DR-29, re-checked, still open). The only on-cable 'flowing' cue should be the current pulses on a closed loop. Those are correct: they only run when the load is on (game.ts:305, Pulses).
- The sprint-overstretch trick is still undiscoverable (M9).
notes.clarity:
Strain reads from the camera from yellow upward:
- orange and red are unmistakable in the big Meeting room (cable-64/65);
- the gold 'connected' tint plus the gold HUD bar clearly mark success (cable-67, cable-85).

At rest, the cream hose on the cream Playground concrete is the least saturated thing near Pip (measured luma 232 vs 191–212 for the floor, saturation 0.09 vs 0.17). Yellow strain on Lunch's honey wood blends in (cable-130).

The spool is readable at the start (cable-02/03), but the reel is off-screen once you are far enough for length to matter. The HUD reel meter carries that information, so it is fine.

Three separate strain threshold tables mean the HUD bar, the hose colour and the prompt don't agree.
